title: ipairs()
summary: Iterates the array part of a table in order: indices 1..n. Stops at the first hole. In Luau you can usually iterate arrays directly without calling it.

details.heading: Behavior
details.body: Yields (index, value) pairs for 1, 2, 3, ... and stops at the first nil. A table with a hole ({1, nil, 3}) stops at index 1.

details.heading: Luau shortcut
details.body: Luau lets you write `for i, v in t` directly for arrays — same behavior, slightly faster. `ipairs` remains useful for clarity and for iterators-as-values.

explanation.whatItIs: The ordered array walker. Give it a list, get back each index and value from first to last.
explanation.whyItExists: Before Luau's direct iteration, this was *the* way to walk an array safely and in order.
whenToUse: Any time you need both the index and the value, in order
When you want to signal 'this is an array' explicitly to readers
whenNotToUse: For dictionaries — `ipairs` sees no array part and loops zero times
On tables with holes — iteration stops early
tips: `for i, v in t` (Luau) ≡ `for i, v in ipairs(t)` for arrays
Need reverse order? Use numeric for: `for i = #t, 1, -1 do`
commonMistakes: Using ipairs on a dictionary and wondering why nothing prints
Relying on it over sparse arrays

examples.title: Walking an array in order
examples.code:
local racers = {"Turbo", "Blaze", "Pixel"}

for i, name in ipairs(racers) do
    print(`#{i}: {name}`)
end
--> #1: Turbo
--> #2: Blaze
--> #3: Pixel
